claims.text: Preformed FeCrAl alloy parts can resist erosion during long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum in hot-dip plating.
FeCrAl alloy forms a continuous alumina (Al2O3) scale under hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
The alumina scale formed on FeCrAl is self-healing.
The alumina scale acts as a protective barrier against erosion by molten aluminum.
The proposed FeCrAl alloy contains sufficient aluminum and chromium to provide the claimed protection.
The as-fabricated FeCrAl alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The molten-aluminum bath operates at approximately 660°C.
Exposure to the molten-aluminum plating environment causes in situ formation of a dense alumina layer on the FeCrAl surface.
The in situ alumina layer adheres to the FeCrAl surface.
High aluminum and chromium contents in FeCrAl promote high-temperature oxidation that develops a continuous alumina scale.
The alumina scale is chemically stable in molten aluminum.
The alumina scale reduces direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying FeCrAl metal.
Reducing direct molten-aluminum contact significantly reduces erosion of the underlying FeCrAl.
FeCrAl parts will have lower erosion rates than conventional steels or alloys that do not form a protective scale.
FeCrAl parts will lose less material than conventional steels or non-scale-forming alloys under comparable plating conditions.
FeCrAl parts will have a longer service life than conventional steels or non-scale-forming alloys.
Carbon steels and low-alloy steels undergo rapid erosion during unprotected contact with molten aluminum.
Protection depends on process temperature, exposure time, and thermal cycling permitting reliable formation and maintenance of the alumina scale.
Severe mechanical or thermal stresses can damage the alumina scale and compromise protection.
